judged_text: createEvent builds the events URL from only destinationCalendar[0].externalId, ignoring which member's credential the service instance authenticates as. For a multi-host collective booking with Office365 hosts, each per-destination createEvent call posts to /me/calendars/{first-host-externalId}/events under the other hosts' tokens — targeting the wrong host's calendar or 404ing — so members' own destination calendars never receive the event.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now loops over all destinations/credentials, calling `createEvent(...)` per host. However, `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` still derives its `eventsUrl` from only the first destination calendar (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` then `/me/calendars/${mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId}/events`). There is no logic to select the destination calendar matching the authenticated credential (unlike the Google service which now selects by `credentialId`). As a result, for multi-host collective scenarios where `event.destinationCalendar` contains multiple calendars, every Office365 createEvent call will target the first calendar externalId regardless of which host token is used, potentially writing to the wrong calendar or 404ing.
